closed_items.resolution: schema-neutral state_storage.py now owns path, lock, timestamp, private-file and atomic-write primitives; Native Core state no longer imports the retired V3 orchestration engine; the 1.0.0 clean break removes the retired stale-state cleanup implementation instead of carrying it as a compatibility path

items.current_condition: Doctor can validate caller-supplied Native Host capability evidence, but ordinary users do not yet have a simple product-owned capture flow
items.target: Use N0-N8 Host observations to decide whether a smaller evidence-capture UX is justified without introducing another runtime control plane

items.current_condition: scripts/calibration_profiles_core.py still contains the original Reader-oriented evaluator transaction implementation, while calibration_profiles.py generalizes it to all roles by replacing selected core functions at import/runtime; these helpers are excluded from runtime package integrity and have no production routing, lifecycle, Doctor, or release authority
items.target: After V4 release-critical Native Core and exact-candidate Host validation stabilize, consolidate calibration profile transactions behind one role-neutral evaluator implementation without changing frozen experiment evidence or production policy

items.current_condition: state_storage.py rejects pre-existing symlinks, confines state under the OS temporary directory, uses private per-thread directories, O_NOFOLLOW for the lock where supported, regular-file fstat checks, bounded files, fsync, and atomic replace; directory and state-path validation still precede later path-based operations, leaving a narrow same-user namespace-swap window when an attacker can mutate that namespace concurrently
items.target: If the supported threat model expands to hostile same-user namespace mutation, evaluate descriptor-relative POSIX operations such as dir_fd/openat with O_NOFOLLOW and fstat plus platform-specific Windows handling and dedicated race tests; do not add this complexity to release-critical Native Core without evidence that the stronger containment boundary is required

release_policy: Open P2 experiment/diagnostic usability debt and P3 storage hardening debt do not replace or relax the exact-candidate N0-N8 Host release gate. Any debt that changes Native Core runtime semantics must be resolved before candidate-bound Host evidence is considered final; P3 hardening remains nonblocking unless the supported threat model is expanded to require hostile same-user namespace containment.
